To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
subdoses of dicamba herbicide on sensitive soybean cultivars, during its vegetative stage (V3) can reduce soybean grain yield.
dicamba herbicide at subdoses of 1.4 g ha-1, 2.7 g ha-1 and 5.6 g ha-1 did not affect soybean yield components, but subdoses above 11.2 g ha-1 caused significant reduction of yield in both stages.
subdoses of dicamba herbicide on sensitive soybean cultivar during its reproductive stages can affect yield components.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effect of dicamba on soybean yield componentes, and it was found that the subdoses of dicamba can reduce the number of pods, grains per pod, grain yield, and the 100-grain weight of sensitive soybean.
the effects of subdoses of the herbicide dicamba at two growth stages of sensitive soybean.
the effect of subdoses of the herbicide dicamba in the V3 and the R2 soybean growth stages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dicamba herbicide, at low doses, is able to affect yield components of sensitive soybean cultivars at the vegetative and reproductive growth stages.
dicamba is a herbicide with potential for use in soybean crops, but the use should be limited to the R2 growth stage and the subdose should be no greater than 11.2 g ae ha-
the herbicide dicamba, in the doses applied in the present work, negatively affected the soybean yield componentes in both the V3 and the R2 stages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dicamba herbicide can cause injury to soybean, especially at the R2 growth stage.
the soybean cultivars without dicamba tolerance are more susceptible to dicamba herbicide injury, especially at R2 growth stage.

the subdoses of the herbicide dicamba can cause injury to soybean plants at the R2 growth stage, with a reduction in the number of nodes and grain yield, and that the herbicide is more toxic to the plants at the R1 and R2 reproductive stages.

the dicamba application at the V3 stage of soybean is more harmful to yield components, compared with the application at the R2 stage, and that the soybean cultivars are more sensitive to the herbicide at the R2 growth stage.
